newsitem.title: GERMANY: German institutes see small rate rise in 1998.
newsitem.headline: German institutes see small rate rise in 1998.

text.p: Germany's six leading economic institutes said on Tuesday they expected the Bundesbank to keep interest rates on hold in 1997 unless there was a sharp rise in the dollar.
But they added that they did see the central bank implementing a small rise in rates early next year.
"The Bundesbank will keep its short-term interest rates at the current level this year," the institutes said in their spring report.
They added: "After the turn of the year official interest rates will be raised slightly. Long-term interest rates will climb slightly this year and next."

Germany's discount and Lombard rates have been on hold at 2.50 percent and 4.50 percent respectively since April last year, while the key money market tender repurchase rate, the repo, has been at three percent last August.
